subject: soda
title: What If You Always Drank Soda Instead of Water?

scenes.text: What if you always drank soda instead of water? You'd stay hydrated. That's not the problem.
Swap six glasses of water for six cans and you'd add roughly 900 calories a day, almost all sugar.
With every sip, acid and sugar wash over your teeth. Lab studies show soft drinks dissolve tooth enamel.
Within a year, even one can a day with no other changes can add up to about five pounds.
Over years, one to two cans a day is linked to about 26 percent higher type 2 diabetes risk.
And the World Health Organization's ideal limit is about six teaspoons of sugar a day. One can holds up to ten.

description:
What if you always drank soda instead of water? A typical can has about 150 calories and up to 40 grams of sugar; soft drinks erode tooth enamel, and one to two a day is linked to about 26% higher type 2 diabetes risk.
The WHO suggests ideally keeping free sugars to about 25 grams (6 teaspoons) a day.
